title: Cohort Retention Index and Sprint Synthesis for Developer Experience Programs
creator: Aisha Khatri
description:
Goal: Define and operationalize a Cohort Retention Index (CRI) for SDKs, docs, and quickstarts and fold the index into our sprint synthesis so product decisions are driven by retention signal rather than vanity metrics.

Scope:
- Establish cohort definitions across sign-up flow, SDK install, first successful request, and first paid request.
- Build weekly CRI dashboards with breakouts by sample cohort window (7d/30d/90d) and by channel (self-serve, partner, internal).
- Run two controlled experiments for quickstart variants (A: guided CLI path, B: sample app with preseeded keys) and measure CRI delta.
- Create a sprint synthesis template so every dx initiative includes CRI, activation funnel, and regression checks.

Why this matters: Current activation metrics (created projects, token usage) mask post-onboarding churn. CRI will surface where users drop off after the first hour, day, and week so we can prioritize changes that increase long-term activation and reduce support load.

Constraints and trade-offs:
- Telemetry cost vs signal: we will sample detailed event payloads for cohorts >1000 to control costs.
- Privacy: exclude PII and store only hashed identifiers for cohort joins; legal reviewed approach is linked in artifacts.
- Accuracy vs time-to-insight: start with a 7-day rolling CRI and iterate to include 30/90 day windows once event pipelines are validated.

Deliverables:
1) CRI spec doc and cohort definitions.
2) Dashboard in Looker with filters, cohort comparison, and cohort-level SLOs.
3) Two quickstart A/B experiment results and PRs to promote winning pattern to templates.
4) Sprint synthesis template and playbook to attach to all future DX tickets.

Acceptance criteria:
- Cohort definitions are published in Confluence and approved by Data & Legal.
- Looker dashboard shows CRI for 7d and 30d windows for last 6 weeks and supports channel filters.
- Experiment 1 and 2 have clear metrics, runbook, and recorded results in the synthesis doc.
- Template adopted by at least 3 active DX squads in the first two cycles.

acceptance_criteria: Published cohort spec with event names and hashed_id strategy approved by Legal
Looker dashboard deployed with 7d and 30d CRI tiles and filter by channel
Two quickstart experiments executed with sample size >= 400 per arm or statistical stopping rules documented
Sprint synthesis template used in end-of-sprint reviews for at least 3 DX initiatives
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: High telemetry cost if detailed event capture is enabled for all users — Mitigation: sampling and pre-aggregation for high volume cohorts
Risk: Misaligned cohort definitions across squads — Mitigation: central spec and automated validation tests in CI
Risk: Experiment inconclusive due to low traffic — Mitigation: extend experiment duration and seed via newsletters/partners
